evidence: Juv. 6.347–348: pōne seram, cohibē. sed quis custōdiet ipsōs custōdēs?
terms.comment: Juvenal, of a husband who sets guards on his wife: who will guard the guards themselves? Some editors reject the lines there; they come again in a passage found in one manuscript, with custōdiat.
Traupman’s shortening of Juvenal’s question, without ipsōs.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Juvenal 6.347–348, checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
